subject: ancient English oak tree in winter, bare of leaves: a massive gnarled trunk with flared buttress roots, burrs and a hollow scar, rising a third of its height before parting into five heavy crooked limbs that twist outward and upward in a broad rounded outline, each limb dividing into a few smaller crooked branches that end thick, as thick as a wrist, with no fine twigs; deeply fissured grey-brown bark with patches of green moss low down
